evidence.summary: Across 768 rows of proper softmax distributions at V=16..4096 and temperatures 0.3/1.0/5.0, kernel output matched argmax(max(t-d,0)*inv_q) exactly (mismatch=0) and never returned a token with negative residual (violations=0). The only mismatches (5) came from a hand-built near-equal case, and in exactly those 5 rows there were zero positive residuals (rows_with_no_positive_residual=5), a configuration impossible for two normalized distributions (sum(t-d)=0). Identical-distribution case matched too. So the missing clamp was not yet shown to matter on admissible inputs.

data.expected_signal: If the missing clamp matters on admissible inputs, case A/B/C shows mismatch>0 with neg_resid_returned>0 while rows_no_positive_resid==0. If all cases show mismatch=0, the clamp is a provable no-op and c1 is rebutted.

evidence.summary: Four adversarial configurations (256 rows each, all rows proper normalized distributions, row sums ~1.0) designed specifically to expose the missing max(.,0) clamp: (A) uniform target vs draft peaked 0.99 on token 0 with inv_q=1e6 placed exactly on that hugely-negative-residual token; (B) inv_q scaled x1e5 on every negative-residual token and x1e-3 on positive ones; (C) target==draft except a single +1e-6 residual, with inv_q=1e6 everywhere except that token; (D) exact-tie stress. In all four: mismatch=0 vs argmax(max(t-d,0)*inv_q), neg_resid_returned=0, rows_no_positive_resid=0. This matches the mathematical argument: for two normalized rows sum(t-d)=0, so either some residual is strictly positive (and with inv_q>0 any positive-residual score strictly exceeds every negative-residual score, making the clamp a no-op for the argmax) or t==d exactly, in which case all clamped scores are 0 and both kernel and reference return index 0 (verified in t7). The omitted clamp is therefore unobservable on contract-admissible inputs.

rationale: Line 23 computes prob = target_prob - draft_prob without clamping to 0; contract states over-proposed tokens carry zero residual probability and must never be returned. Need to determine whether unclamped argmax can actually differ from clamped argmax on admissible inputs.

scope_evidence.summary: Requires p_residual = max(target-draft,0), returns argmax(p_residual*inv_q), and explicitly forbids returning a token with target_prob<draft_prob.

scope_rationale: problem.txt states the residual distribution is p_residual(v) ∝ max(target_prob[v]-draft_prob[v],0) and that the kernel must return argmax_v(p_residual(v)*inv_q[v]), with over-proposed tokens never returned. Any input consisting of two per-row probability distributions plus positive inv_q is admissible.
statement: The kernel omits the required max(target_prob - draft_prob, 0) clamp, so for inputs the contract admits (target_probs/draft_probs rows that are probability distributions, inv_q>0) it can return a token v with target_prob[v] < draft_prob[v], i.e. a zero-residual token, disagreeing with argmax_v(max(t-d,0)*inv_q).

evidence.summary: On a Tesla T4, vocab sizes 4096, 8192, 32000, 32768, 50257 and 128256 (BLOCK_SIZE up to 131072) all compiled and ran without error, and every case matched the clamped reference argmax exactly (mismatch=0) with no negative-residual token returned. Non-power-of-two vocab sizes (32000, 50257, 128256) exercise the masking path correctly. The BLOCK_SIZE=next_power_of_2(vocab_size) choice does not break at realistic vocabularies.

rationale: Line 38 makes the block cover the whole vocab in one iteration, so three fp32 tensors of up to 131072 lanes are materialized per program; this may exceed Triton resource limits.

data.expected_signal: If the kernel violates the invariant at scale, mismatch>0 / neg_resid_returned>0 with rows_no_positive_resid==0. All-zero counts rebut c3.

evidence.summary: At V=32000 and V=128256 with normalized rows (row sums 0.9999999-1.0000001) engineered to contain exactly one positive residual (median_npos=1) and inv_q scaled x1e6 on every negative-residual token while the single positive-residual token got inv_q=1e-6, the kernel returned exactly the reference argmax(max(t-d,0)*inv_q) in all 32 rows (mismatch=0, neg_resid_returned=0, rows_no_positive_resid=0); e.g. at V=128256 kernel_tok0=ref_tok0=idx0=103074, and at V=32000 kernel_tok0=ref_tok0=idx0=17954. Two additional realistic batches (B=64, plain Exponential(1) inv_q, sharper softmax) at V=32000 and V=128256 also matched exactly with int64 output of shape [B]. c3 is rebutted: the kernel recovers the correct token even when the race is maximally biased toward forbidden tokens at full-vocabulary scale.

rationale: This is the hardest admissible configuration for the unclamped score: the correct token's score is ~1e-6 * small inv_q while 32k negative-residual tokens carry inv_q up to 1e6. It simultaneously exercises the boundary masking at non-power-of-two V and any fp32 cancellation in target-draft. Confirmation would reject; rebuttal, combined with the c1/c2 evidence, supports trust.

scope_evidence.summary: Contract fixes the output as argmax_v(p_residual(v)*inv_q[v]) with p_residual = max(target-draft,0) and forbids returning any token with target_prob < draft_prob.
Operation is vllm's sample_recovered_tokens over an LLM vocabulary, so vocab sizes such as 32000/128256 are representative of the declared domain.

scope_rationale: problem.txt states the kernel must return argmax_v(max(target-draft,0)*inv_q) and that an over-proposed token (target<draft) must never be returned. Rows that are proper probability distributions with a single small positive residual, plus inv_q = 1/Exponential(1) values, are exactly the input class the contract declares; vocabulary size is chosen from the LLM vocab sizes the cited vllm operator operates on.
statement: At realistic vocabulary sizes (32000, 128256) with normalized target/draft rows containing exactly one tiny positive residual among tens of thousands of negative residuals, and inv_q biased heavily toward the negative-residual tokens, the kernel returns a token with target_prob < draft_prob (violating the contract invariant) or disagrees with argmax(max(t-d,0)*inv_q).
